notes: The GRAIL Q2'26 10-Q is reachable on EDGAR with no login, but it adds little that is new. Galleri volumes were already known (>117K in H1'26, +42%). The 10-Q gives no Illumina pricing, minimum or MFN terms, and no per-test cost or sequencer commentary. I read one excerpt of the Q2'26 10-Q (offset 60000, via a summarizing fetch). I did not read the FY25 10-K or the Q1'26 10-Q. The royalty terms, the 'cost of screening revenue' figure and the ASP/volume figures all came from that excerpt. The only new item is the royalty restart date, and it has little bearing on the thesis. The 10-Q's original text on the royalty could not be confirmed beyond that excerpt.
how_to_mine: Open the GRAIL FY25 10-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1699031/000162828026017319/gral-20251231.htm) and check the Risk Factors and Related Party sections. Look for the Illumina supply and sole-source terms, and for the Exhibit 10 list, where the 2024 amendments to the supply agreement may be filed with redactions. The Form 10 Ex. 10.6 and the 4th amendment were already used. Also check the Q2'26 10-Q commitments note for purchase obligations to Illumina. Compute cost of screening revenue per test for each quarter from the 10-Qs. That figure includes lab costs, so it is not a sequencing-only number.

items.label: 1B
items.claim: GRAIL's Illumina royalty (suspended since 2024) resumes 24 Dec 2026 unless GRAIL changes control, with a 7% effective floor and a 5% rate after $1B cumulative.
items.detail: The Q2'26 10-Q says the 9% oncology royalty is suspended until 24 Dec 2026. Anti-stacking can lower it to a 7% floor, which GRAIL expects to be its effective rate. This is a new Illumina revenue stream starting in Q1'27, but it is a royalty, not consumables pricing, and it is small relative to the scale of the thesis. It does not show price pressure and is more neutral than supportive. Q2'26 Galleri volume rose 35% y/y while ASP fell 8%. Cost of screening revenue was $23.3M in Q2'26 and $44.6M for H1'26, which is roughly $380 per test on about 61K tests, including all lab costs.
items.quote: suspended until December 24, 2026 or any earlier change of control
items.why_new: The royalty restart date and the screening cost per test are not in the known list. The volume figures are already known.
